items.prompt: In a clocked always block, non-blocking (<=) means…
choices: All RHS values are sampled first, then LHS updates happen together
Statements never run on a clock edge
items.explain: NBA uses pre-edge values for every RHS, then applies all updates at once.

items.prompt: q1 = d; q2 = q1; on one posedge (blocking) typically…
choices: Both q1 and q2 get d in the same edge
q2 gets the old q1 from the previous cycle only
items.explain: Blocking runs in order—q2 sees the new q1 after q1 = d in the same edge.

items.prompt: a <= b; b <= a; on one posedge (non-blocking) with a=1, b=0 before the edge…
choices: a becomes 0 and b becomes 1 — a real swap
items.explain: Both RHS values are sampled before any update, so a and b trade.

items.prompt: Flip-flop RTL in always @(posedge clk) should normally use <= for register updates.
items.explain: Non-blocking is the standard sequential style; blocking can infer unexpected combo paths.
